simple.meaning: עָמִיר (ʻâmîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “a bunch of grain.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עָמִיר (H5995) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 9:21, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Amos, Micah, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָמִיר (H5995) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עָמִיר (H5995) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עָמִיר (ʻâmîyr) / H5995 is traced through Jeremiah 9:21, Amos 2:13, Micah 4:12, Zechariah 12:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For death has come up into our windows.

timeline.evidenceText: For death has come up into our windows.
Behold,† “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. I will crush you in your place,
But they don’t know the thoughts of Yahweh,

In that day I will make the chieftains of Judah like a pan of fire among wood, and like a flaming torch among sheaves; and they will devour all the surrounding peoples, on the right hand and on the left; and Jerusalem will yet again dwell in their own place, even in Jerusalem.

definitions.full: H5995. amir עָמִיר noun [masculine] swath, row of fallen grain ( hay , as Mishna, according to Vogelst l.c. 74 f. (who is then compelled to read עֹמֶר Micah 4:12 ), compare Syriac grass , Schw Idioticon 69 ); — Amos 2:13 (on cart), Jer 9:21 (falling behind reaper), Micah 4:12 (brought to threshing-floor), Zech 12:6 (inflammable).
